chapters.chapterDescription: Master the building blocks of digital electronics! Learn how simple gates like AND, OR, and XOR form the foundation of all computer logic. By combining these basic gates, you'll create increasingly powerful circuits that perform complex operations.

levels.name: NOT Gate
levels.description: Output should be the inverse of input.

levels.name: AND Gate
levels.description: Output should be 1 only if both inputs are 1.

levels.name: OR Gate
levels.description: Output should be 1 if either input is 1.

levels.name: XOR Gate
levels.description: Output should be 1 if exactly one input is 1.

levels.name: NOR Gate
levels.description: Output is 1 only when both inputs are 0.
hints: NOR is NOT OR
Y = NOT (A OR B)

levels.name: XNOR Gate
levels.description: Output is 1 when inputs are equal.

chapters.chapterDescription: Building upon basic logic gates, these challenges introduce more complex combinational circuits, multi-input functions, and fundamental functional blocks. Master the art of combining simple gates to create sophisticated logic operations.

levels.name: A AND NOT B
levels.description: Output should be 1 when A=1 and B=0.

levels.name: A OR NOT B
levels.description: Output should be 1 when A=1 or B=0 (or both).

levels.name: Implication (A → B)
levels.description: (!A) OR B.

levels.name: 3-Input AND
levels.description: Output is 1 only when A=B=C=1.

levels.name: 3-Input OR
levels.description: Output is 1 if any input is 1.

levels.name: Majority
levels.description: Output is 1 when at least two inputs are 1.

levels.name: Parity (Odd, 3-bit)
levels.description: Output is 1 when the number of 1s is odd.

levels.name: At Least One Zero
levels.description: Output is 1 unless both inputs are 1.

levels.name: 2→1 MUX (S,A,B)
levels.description: If S=0 output A; if S=1 output B.

chapters.chapterDescription: Enter the world of memory and time! Build circuits that remember their past and create counters, latches, and flip-flops. This is where digital circuits gain the power of memory and state.

levels.name: SR Latch
levels.description: Basic memory element. Set when S=1, Reset when R=1, Hold when both are 0.
hints: Use NAND gates
Q = NOT (R AND Qn)
Qn = NOT (S AND Q)

levels.name: D Latch
levels.description: Level-triggered memory element. When Enable=1, Q follows D. When Enable=0, Q holds its value (latched).
hints: D Latch is level-triggered, not edge-triggered
When Enable=1: Q becomes D immediately (transparent mode)
When Enable=0: Q holds its current value (latch mode)
Can be built using NAND gates or an SR Latch with D and NOT D inputs
Q' is always the complement of Q

levels.name: D Flip-Flop
levels.description: Data storage element. Q follows D on rising clock edge. Q' is the complement of Q. When CLK goes high, Q captures the value of D and holds it until the next rising edge.
hints: D flip-flop stores the D input on rising clock edge
Q changes only when CLK transitions from 0 to 1
Q' (Q complement) is always the opposite of Q
Characteristic equation: Q(n+1) = D(n)

chapters.chapterDescription: Learn the magic of binary math! Construct adders from simple gates, understand carry propagation, and build the mathematical foundation that powers every computer's arithmetic unit.

levels.name: Half Adder
levels.description: Add two single bits. Output is sum and carry.
hints: Sum = A XOR B
Carry = A AND B

levels.name: 4-bit Adder
levels.description: Add two 4-bit numbers. Output is 5-bit result (4-bit sum + carry).

chapters.chapterDescription: Reach the pinnacle of digital design! Build subtraction circuits using two's complement, create comparators, and finally construct a complete ALU - the heart of every processor that performs all arithmetic and logic operations.

levels.name: 4-bit Subtractor
levels.description: Subtract B from A using two's complement. Output is difference and borrow.
hints: Use two's complement: A - B = A + (~B + 1)
Invert B, add 1, then use 4-bit adder
Borrow indicates negative result

levels.name: 4-bit Comparator
levels.description: Compare two 4-bit numbers. Output A>B, A=B, A<B.
hints: A = B when all bits match
A > B when MSB differs and A_MSB=1, or MSB same and A > B in lower bits
A < B when neither A > B nor A = B
Compare bits from most significant to least significant

levels.name: Simple ALU (Add/Sub)
levels.description: 4-bit ALU with add/subtract operations. Op=0: add, Op=1: subtract.

levels.name: Complete 4-bit ALU
levels.description: Full ALU with 4 operations: AND, OR, ADD, SUB. 2-bit operation select.

levels.name: 4-bit Counter
levels.description: Count from 0 to 15 and repeat. Use clock input.

chapters.chapterDescription: Bridge the gap between simple logic gates and real-world computing! Learn to work with 8-bit data buses - the fundamental unit of computer memory. Master parallel processing, understand carry propagation across bytes, and build circuits that manipulate data the way real processors do. From simple operations to a complete 8-bit ALU, you'll discover how computers process information at the byte level.

levels.name: 8-Bit Wire
levels.description: Connect the 8-bit input directly to the 8-bit output. This introduces the concept of multi-bit buses - bundles of wires that carry parallel data signals. Think of it as moving an entire byte of information at once!
hints: Connect A0 to OUT0, A1 to OUT1, and so on...
This is the simplest 8-bit operation - just passing data through

levels.name: 8-Bit 2-to-1 Multiplexer
levels.description: Build an 8-bit 2-to-1 multiplexer. When SEL=0, output A; when SEL=1, output B. This circuit selects between two 8-bit data sources based on a single control signal.

levels.name: 8-Bit Adder
levels.description: Add two 8-bit numbers with carry-in and carry-out. This is real binary arithmetic! The carry ripples through all 8 bits, just like carrying in decimal addition.

levels.name: 8-Bit Equality Comparator
levels.description: Compare two 8-bit numbers for equality. Output 1 if A equals B, 0 otherwise. All 8 bits must match! This is how computers check if two values are the same.
hints: A equals B when all bits match
Use XNOR for each bit pair, then AND all results together
Or: XOR each bit pair, OR all results, then NOT the final output

levels.name: 8-Bit Greater Than
levels.description: Compare two 8-bit unsigned numbers. Output 1 if A > B, 0 otherwise. Start comparing from the most significant bit (MSB) - just like comparing decimal numbers from left to right!

levels.name: 8-Bit Left Shifter
levels.description: Shift all bits left by 1 position. Bit 7 receives bit 6, bit 6 receives bit 5, and so on. Bit 0 becomes 0. Fun fact: shifting left by 1 is the same as multiplying by 2!
hints: Connect IN6 to OUT7, IN5 to OUT6, etc.
OUT0 is always 0
This is just wire routing - no gates needed!

levels.name: 8-Bit Incrementer
levels.description: Add 1 to the 8-bit input. This is a special case of addition used everywhere in computers - incrementing program counters, array indices, loop counters, etc.
hints: This is adding 1 to the input
You can use an 8-bit adder with B=00000001 and Cin=0
Or chain full adders with the first Cin=1 and all B inputs=0

levels.name: 8-Bit ALU
levels.description: Build an 8-bit Arithmetic Logic Unit with 4 operations selected by 2 control bits (OP-0, OP-1): 00=bitwise-AND, 01=bitwise-OR, 10=ADD, 11=SUB. Combine everything you've learned into a real data processing unit!
